examBlueprint.tests: B4.3: the mitochondrion with stages placed, or the electron transport chain
Interpreting scientific text; passage drawn from B4.4 (the respiration passage)

standards.title: Redox and the overview of respiration
standards.titleAsPrinted: Redox and the Overview of Respiration
standards.description: Students explain how respiration releases energy through redox and name the stages.
iCan: I can define oxidation (loss of electrons) and reduction (gain of electrons), and explain that electrons carry energy
I can identify NAD+ and FAD as electron carriers that become NADH and FADH2 and shuttle electrons to the electron transport chain
I can write and explain the overall equation: glucose plus oxygen yields carbon dioxide plus water plus ATP
I can name the three stages and where each happens, and label the mitochondrion (matrix, cristae, intermembrane space)

standards.title: Glycolysis
standards.description: Students explain how glycolysis begins to harvest energy from glucose.
iCan: I can state that glycolysis splits one glucose (6 carbons) into two pyruvate (3 carbons)
I can explain that glycolysis happens in the cytoplasm and needs no oxygen, which is why it is universal and ancient
I can account for the energy: invest 2 ATP, make 4 (net 2 ATP) by substrate-level phosphorylation, plus 2 NADH
I can explain that the pyruvate and NADH carry energy on to the later stages (or to fermentation if no oxygen)

standards.title: Pyruvate oxidation and the citric acid cycle
standards.titleAsPrinted: Pyruvate Oxidation and the Citric Acid Cycle
standards.description: Students explain how the citric acid cycle completes the oxidation of glucose.
iCan: I can explain that pyruvate is oxidized to acetyl-CoA, releasing one CO2 and making one NADH per pyruvate
I can state that the citric acid cycle runs in the mitochondrial matrix
I can give the per-turn tally: 2 CO2, 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, and 1 ATP, with two turns per glucose
I can explain that the main payoff here is the loaded carriers (NADH, FADH2), and that exhaled CO2 comes from these steps

exam.examItems: MC Q5, Q6; SA 15; Part 4 Diagram

standards.title: Oxidative phosphorylation (electron transport and chemiosmosis)
standards.description: Students explain how the electron transport chain and chemiosmosis make most of the ATP.
iCan: I can explain that NADH and FADH2 drop electrons into the chain, which fall to oxygen, the final electron acceptor, forming water
I can explain how the energy released pumps H+ into the intermembrane space, building a gradient
I can explain chemiosmosis: H+ flows back through ATP synthase, which makes ATP
I can state that this stage makes most of the ATP (about 28), and that without oxygen the whole chain stops

standards.title: Fermentation and anaerobic respiration
standards.description: Students explain how cells make ATP without oxygen.
iCan: I can explain that without oxygen the electron transport chain stops, so NADH cannot be unloaded
I can explain that fermentation regenerates NAD+ so glycolysis can keep making 2 ATP
I can tell lactic acid fermentation (muscle, makes lactate) from alcohol fermentation (yeast, makes ethanol and CO2)
I can compare yields: about 32 ATP per glucose with oxygen versus only 2 by fermentation
